title: Koszul tensor and tail comparisons preserve Roos projection adjoints
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $t$ a global section such that multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is injective. Put $B_m=R/t^mR$ and $K_m=[R\xrightarrow{t^m}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, augmented to $B_m$, for $m\geq1$. Let $X_\bullet$ be a strict inverse sequence of unbounded $R$-complexes and let $H=R\!\lim_nX_n$ with its projections $p_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Countable products of $R$-modules are exact and derived products are represented termwise; write $\mathsf R(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod X_n\to\prod X_n)[-1]$ for the Roos model [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For every $h\geq1$, deleting the levels $n<h$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $\mathsf R(X)\to\mathsf R(X|_{n\geq h})$ compatible with the remaining projections. The canonical tensor/product and cone identifications give a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R\to B_m}(H\otimes_R^LB_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\!\lim_{n\geq h}(X_n\otimes_RK_m)$$
in $D(R)$, where $K_m$ computes the restricted derived tensor. Under it, the projection to $X_n\otimes_RK_m$ is the derived tensor of $p_n$, with the canonical two-term comparison.

More precisely, fix $h=m$, a complex $N$ of $B_m$-modules and a strict compatible family of $B_m$-linear chain maps $f_n:X_n\otimes_RB_m\to N$ for $n\geq m$. Compose the last isomorphism with the derived limit of the augmentations $X_n\otimes_RK_m\to X_n\otimes_RB_m$, then with $R\!\lim f_n$ and the diagonal identification $R\!\lim\operatorname{const}(N)\cong N$. The resulting morphism is the restriction of the adjoint, under the derived tensor--restriction adjunction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], of $H\xrightarrow{p_m}X_m\to\operatorname{Res}N$, the second map being $x\mapsto f_m(x\otimes1)$. Restriction to $D(R)$ detects isomorphisms in $D(B_m)$. These identifications commute with the coefficient quotient transitions: for $k\leq m$ the Koszul transition $K_m\to K_k$ is $(t^{m-k},1)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$. Finally, if all $X_n$ have cohomology in one interval $[a,b]$, then $H$ has cohomology in $[a,b+1]$, without a quasi-compactness hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Proof paragraph, repleteness and finite-tail deletion; reduction as a two-term cone commuting with Rlim; naturality; boundedness; returned DAG proof steps 3, 7, 8, 11; Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes, §3.5, Lemmas 3.5.4–3.5.7.

proof.text: Work on the small pro-étale site in a module universe containing its objects. Countable products of $R$-module sheaves are sectionwise and exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], for arbitrary $T$. Exactness implies $H^q(\prod X_n)=\prod H^q(X_n)$: the product functor preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology. Choose individual K-injective resolutions using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Their product represents the derived product by [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective], and the map from the product of the original complexes is a quasi-isomorphism by the preceding cohomology equality. Thus termwise products represent derived products. The normalized natural comparison [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies the strict Roos fibre with the actual $H=R\!\lim X_\bullet$, carries its coordinate maps to $p_n$, and identifies strict maps of Roos fibres with derived-limit maps. We use this normalization throughout, also after reindexing a tail by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}$.

source.place: Propositions 3.1.9, 3.2.3(1), 4.2.8; Stacks sites-cohomology Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), derived Tag 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective).

proof.text: Fix the following coordinates, using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a chain endomorphism $u:P\to P$, write $F_u^q=P^q\oplus P^{q-1}$ with $d(x,y)=(dx,ux-dy)$. The map $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$ identifies this with $\operatorname{Cone}(u)[-1]$; projection is $(x,y)\mapsto x$. Put $D_m(C)=C\otimes_RK_m$. In degree $q$ write its coordinates as $(a,b)\in C^q\oplus C^{q+1}$. The total differential is $d(a,b)=(da+(-1)^{q+1}t^m b,db)$. Consequently $(a,b)\mapsto(a,(-1)^{q+1}b)$ is a chain isomorphism $D_m(C)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(t^m:C\to C)$, carrying the inclusion of $C$ to the cone inclusion and the augmentation to $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. These formulas fix all signs used below.

source.place: Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex); derived.tex, cone and shift conventions in section-homotopy-category.

proof.text: Multiplication by $t^m$ is injective, being a composite of $m$ injective maps, and $B_m$ is its sheaf cokernel. Hence $0\to R\xrightarrow{t^m}R\to B_m\to0$ is exact. Apply [lem-cbc-regular-quotient-cone-augmentation] with $r=t^m$ and $S=B_m$. Together with the coordinate isomorphism in step 2 this gives a natural isomorphism $A_{m,C}:QD_m(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}(QC\otimes_R^LB_m)$. For a K-flat $P$, $A_{m,P}$ is represented by the augmentation $P\otimes K_m\to\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes B_m)$, and the inclusion $P\to D_m(P)$ becomes $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. The derived scalar extension is computed on these resolutions by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The same cited cone theorem gives naturality for all derived morphisms and resolution independence. In particular $D_m$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, since its localized cone functor exists on $D(R)$, or directly by the cone cohomology sequence.

source.place: Tag 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism), construction preceding Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), and Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); principal quotient cone model.

proof.text: Delete the coordinates $n<h$ in both copies of the product. This strictly commutes with $1-s$, hence defines $F_{1-s}(\prod_{n\geq1}X_n)\to F_{1-s}(\prod_{n\geq h}X_n)$. It is degreewise split surjective, and its kernel is $F_U(P_{<h})$, where $P_{<h}=\prod_{1\leq n<h}X_n$, $U=1-s_{<h}$, and the shift on the finite prefix has zero last component. It is nilpotent: $s_{<h}^{h-1}=0$ for $h>1$. Thus $U^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^{h-2}s_{<h}^j$. On the kernel the degree $-1$ map $(x,y)\mapsto(U^{-1}y,0)$ satisfies $dH+Hd=1$, since $U$ commutes with $d$. The kernel is therefore acyclic. The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] proves the deletion map is a quasi-isomorphism. For $h=1$ it is the identity and its kernel is zero. Every retained projection is unchanged literally.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), finite-tail invariance in the blueprint proof; explicit finite-prefix contraction; homology.tex Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain).

proof.text: Let $P=\prod_nX_n$. The canonical map $D_m(P)\to\prod_nD_m(X_n)$ is the chain isomorphism $( (a_n)_n,(b_n)_n )\mapsto((a_n,b_n))_n$. Its inverse takes the two coordinate families. This is a sheaf map: products are sectionwise and only two summands occur in every total degree. The differential in step 2 is componentwise, so this permutation commutes with $d$. If $s((a_n))=(v_na_{n+1})$ for the transition maps $v_n$, it also commutes with $s$ and therefore with $1-s$. It commutes with every product projection, all strict tower maps, and deletion of any prefix, as each of these acts on the same coordinates.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), product model, with homology.tex Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex); explicit two-summand calculation.

proof.text:
Tensor the fibre coordinates of step 2. For any $u:P\to P$, a degree $q$ element of $D_m(F_u)$ has coordinates $(x,y,z,w)\in P^q\oplus P^{q-1}\oplus P^{q+1}\oplus P^q$. Send it to $((x,z),(y,w))\in F_{D_m(u)}^q$. Both differentials, in the target ordering, are
$$((dx+(-1)^{q+1}t^m z,dz),(ux-dy+(-1)^{q+1}t^m w,uz-dw)).$$
Thus this permutation is a chain isomorphism $D_m(F_u)\cong F_{D_m(u)}$. It commutes with the first-coordinate projections to $D_m(P)$ and with maps commuting with $u$. Combining it for $u=1-s$ with step 5 gives a natural chain isomorphism $D_m(\mathsf R(X))\cong\mathsf R(D_m(X))$ that retains every projection. No infinite totalization is being interchanged with a product.

source.place: Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex); explicit interchange of two two-term total complexes, expanding the blueprint sentence that reduction is a cone and commutes with Rlim.

proof.text: Represent $H$ by $Q\mathsf R(X)$ using step 1. Start with $A_{m,\mathsf R(X)}^{-1}$ from step 3, apply the chain isomorphism of step 6, delete the prefix by step 4 applied to the strict tower $D_m(X_n)$, and use [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] on that tail. The composite is the asserted isomorphism from $\operatorname{Res}(H\otimes_R^LB_m)$ to $R\!\lim_{n\geq h}D_m(X_n)$. Its composite with projection to level $n$ is $D_m(p_n)$ after $A_m^{-1}$: this holds at chain level in steps 4–6 and for the normalized derived-limit comparison in step 1. Naturality of $A_m$ says exactly that this is the restriction of the derived tensor of $p_n$, followed by the stated two-term comparison.

source.place: First paragraph: reduction is the cone of multiplication and commutes with Rlim; terms with n<m do not affect the limit. Projection normalization expanded using Stacks Tag 0941.

proof.text: For the constant tail $N$, put $P_N=\prod_{n\geq m}N$ and $u=1-s$. Define $v:P_N\to P_N$ by $(vz)_m=0$ and $(vz)_n=-\sum_{j=m}^{n-1}z_j$ for $n>m$. These are finite sums, so define sheaf maps and commute with $d$. One has $uv=1$ and $x=\operatorname{diag}(x_m)+vux$. Hence $P_N\cong N\oplus P_N$ by $x\mapsto(x_m,ux)$, and $F_u\cong N\oplus F_{1_{P_N}}$ by $(x,y)\mapsto(x_m,(ux,y))$. The second factor contracts by $(a,b)\mapsto(b,0)$. Therefore $e:F_u\to N$, $(x,y)\mapsto x_m$, is inverse in the derived category to the diagonal $N\to F_u$, $z\mapsto(\operatorname{diag}z,0)$. This fixes the diagonal identification required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), strict Roos model; explicit constant-tower contraction, using only finite coordinate sums.

proof.text:
Now put $h=m$. The augmentations $D_m(X_n)\to X_n\otimes B_m$ commute strictly with transitions. The assumed compatibility of $f_n$ makes their composites $g_n:D_m(X_n)\to\operatorname{Res}N$ a strict map to the constant tail. Under the normalized comparison [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], their derived-limit map is exactly the coordinatewise map of Roos fibres. Applying $e$ from step 8 selects its first product component at $m$. Consequently the complete composite of the statement, on the model $D_m(\mathsf R(X))$, is
$$D_m(\mathsf R(X))\xrightarrow{D_m(p_m)}D_m(X_m)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{aug}}X_m\otimes_RB_m\xrightarrow{f_m}\operatorname{Res}N.$$
This is an equality of the indicated chain maps, not an inference that arbitrary morphisms into a homotopy limit are determined by their projections.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), strict-map naturality; blueprint naturality and finite-tail sentence, expanded at the m-th coordinate.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $q:P\to\mathsf R(X)$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Ordinary scalar extension and restriction on complexes have the specified adjunction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-scalar-extension-complex-adjunction], with unit $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Derive it using [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and exact restriction [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]: kernels and sheafified cokernels have unchanged underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. On $P$, the map $H\to\operatorname{Res}N$ in the statement is represented by $p\mapsto f_m(p_mq(p)\otimes1)$. Its adjoint is represented on $P\otimes B_m$ by $p\otimes b\mapsto b f_m(p_mq(p)\otimes1)$. After the augmentation $D_m(P)\to P\otimes B_m$ this sends $(a,b)$ to $f_m(p_mq(a)\otimes1)$, exactly the map in step 9 precomposed with $D_m(q)$. Both $D_m(q)$ and this augmentation are quasi-isomorphisms, by steps 2–3. The normalization of [lem-cbc-regular-quotient-cone-augmentation] identifies this roof with $A_m^{-1}$. Thus the equality is precisely the restriction of the derived adjoint asserted, including its unit normalization.

Restriction along $R\to B_m$ preserves and reflects vanishing of cohomology: it leaves the underlying abelian sheaves unchanged and is exact, by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and the kernel/cokernel description [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. It is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. If the restriction of a derived morphism $a:A\to B$ is invertible, its cone restricts to zero, so that cone is acyclic and hence zero in the derived category. In the triangle $A\xrightarrow a B\to0\to A[1]$, exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(B,-)$ from [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] supplies $r$ with $ar=1$. In the backward rotation $0[-1]\to A\xrightarrow a B\to0$, the same exactness with source $A$ gives $ra-1=0$ since $a(ra-1)=0$. Thus $a$ is invertible. This proves detection of isomorphisms without asserting faithfulness or fullness of derived restriction.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological); exact faithful underlying-sheaf restriction and the cone criterion.

proof.text: For $k\leq m$, the map $K_m\to K_k$ has components $t^{m-k}$ in degree $-1$ and $1$ in degree $0$. It is a chain map because $t^k t^{m-k}=t^m$, and it commutes with the augmentations via $B_m\to B_k$. On $D_m(C)^q$ it sends $(a,b)$ to $(a,t^{m-k}b)$. On $P\otimes B_m$, for a single K-flat resolution $P$, the corresponding map is $p\otimes\bar r\mapsto p\otimes\bar r$ modulo $t^k$. The augmentation square therefore commutes on both summands. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] these are the coefficient quotient transitions; step 3 identifies their restrictions with the displayed $K$-maps. The permutations in steps 5–6 and tail deletion act on independent coordinates and commute with these maps. Compare different tails on the common tail $n\geq\max(h_m,h_k)$; the deletion maps compose literally. All resulting derived comparison squares commute. For $j\leq k\leq m$ the degree $-1$ components compose because $t^{k-j}t^{m-k}=t^{m-j}$; identity transitions have components $(1,1)$. If compatible target families are also varied, the formulas of steps 9–10 give the corresponding naturality square on the same resolution.

source.place: First paragraph, natural reduction maps and finite tails; Stacks sites-cohomology Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), expanded on the two Koszul components.

proof.text: Finally suppose $H^q(X_n)=0$ for all $q\notin[a,b]$ and all $n$. Exact products give $H^q(P)=\prod_nH^q(X_n)$ as in step 1, so $P=\prod X_n$ has the same cohomological bound. In the Roos triangle $H\to P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\to H[1]$, use [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]: the segment $H^{q-1}(P)\to H^q(H)\to H^q(P)$ has both outside terms zero for $q<a$ or $q>b+1$. Thus $H^q(H)=0$ there, proving the interval $[a,b+1]$. The product exactness statement used here holds for every scheme, and none of the coordinate calculations imposed quasi-compactness on $T$.
